name: DEALER'S CHOICE
description: Dealer's Choice is a popular 'meta-format' for home poker games where the player in the dealer position chooses which specific poker variant will be played for that hand (or round). It emphasizes entertainment, variety, and the ability to adapt to shifting rules, ranging from standard Stud and Draw to eccentric wild-card 'invented' games.

content.text: Dealer's Choice is a popular 'meta-format' for home poker games where the player in the dealer position chooses which specific poker variant will be played for that hand (or round). It emphasizes entertainment, variety, and the ability to adapt to shifting rules, ranging from standard Stud and Draw to eccentric wild-card 'invented' games.

Developed alongside modern Poker as a 'home game' tradition. While casino poker standardized games like Texas Hold'em for efficiency and house edge visibility, social clubs and home games leaned into 'Dealer's Choice' to level the playing field and keep the game fresh.
5-7 players (Ideal: 6). Too many players limit 'Shared Card' or 'Stud' variants; too few make 'Draw' variants less tactical.
Standard 52-card pack. Two packs of different colors are recommended (one being shuffled while the other is in play).
Poker chips, dealer button, reference sheet for complex variants.
The first dealer is chosen randomly. After each variant is complete, the deal passes clockwise.

items.text: Baseball: 7-card stud where 3s and 9s are wild, and 4s give an extra card.
Follow the Queen: 7-card stud where the card dealt after any Queen becomes wild.
Acey Deucey / In-Between: Gambling game often allowed in Dealer's Choice where you bet on a 3rd card falling between two others.
